title: Finite Q3 local-energy modular multiplier envelope for source-boundary Duhamel histories
question: For finite Q3 source-boundary histories B, does the four-leg local-energy norm of [Delta,B] admit an explicit similarity-constant envelope that keeps all noncommuting K and Gibbs modular factors visible?

model.weight: K=I+H-min(spec(H))I, or the analogous local H_X weight, so K>=I
model.similarity_constants: a=||K^(1/2)Delta K^(-1/2)||, b=||rho^(-1/2)Delta rho^(1/2)||, d=||Delta||, e=||K^(-1/2)Delta K^(1/2)||, with adjoint analogues
model.component_bound: Each commutator leg is bounded by (a+b), (a_star+b_star), (d+e), or (d_star+e_star) times the matching B leg
model.total_bound: N_K,rho([Delta,B]) <= Gamma_K,rho(Delta) N_K,rho(B), Gamma=max of the four component coefficients
model.history: B=exp(-i t(H+s Delta)/hbar) A exp(i t(H+s Delta)/hbar), s in the declared finite interpolation grid

adversarial_review.check: K is retained as a full matrix and K^(1/2)K^(-1/2) is inserted only by exact finite multiplication; no simultaneous diagonalization with Delta, B, or rho is assumed.
Both rho^(-1/2)Delta rho^(1/2) and the adjoint orientation are included, so a one-sided Gibbs estimate is not substituted for the four-leg statement.
The right legs use K^(-1/2)Delta K^(1/2) separately from the left similarity constant; no commutation with K is assumed.
The total coefficient is the maximum of the four component sums, and every component inequality is checked before the aggregate envelope is accepted.
Positive finite K and full-rank finite Gibbs rho are checked before inverse square roots; the tiny eigenvalue floor is numerical admissibility only, not a thermodynamic lower bound.
The declared finite volumes, cutoff radii, beta values, interpolation points and both signs are all retained; finite coefficient growth is not called a divergence or a uniform theorem.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator tensors, Q3 onsite/bond matrices, cutoff bonds, Gibbs powers, similarity constants and weighted legs without importing the primary audit.
R344 checks only the nonnegative scalar component aggregation used after the matrix factorization; Python carries the finite matrix spectral calculation and no analytic limit is encoded.

This finite multiplier envelope does not prove modular-domain transfer, source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, a common OS carrier, exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, a GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R344 checks the nonnegative scalar aggregation used when the four finite matrix leg bounds are combined; it does not formalize matrix spectral calculus, modular domains, or QFT limits.

qft_interface.closed: A finite noncommuting local/global energy-weighted multiplier inequality for source-boundary commutators, with explicit left/right Gibbs and energy similarity constants, independent reconstruction and a Lean scalar aggregation check.
qft_interface.open: Uniform control of the similarity constants on the unbounded Q3 common core, modular-domain transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, products, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the explicit similarity constants as the analytic target: derive a source-, volume-, cutoff- and beta-uniform bound on a named unbounded Q3 core, or record a route-local failure if any constant necessarily escapes. Do not promote finite inverse-power data to a common QFT modular estimate.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Q3 modular multiplier checkpoint. It is not a thermodynamic common-Hilbert theorem, a common-alpha construction, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a QFT/Clay closure.
no_overclaim: The package promotes only the finite matrix factorization and component-wise four-leg envelope on the declared rows. It does not prove source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, an unbounded common-core theorem, modular transfer, direct Cauchy convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.
